chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Ja'far who said:

I wrote to the man (Imam asws), asking him asws about a man who bought a camel or a cow for the sacrifice. So when he slaughtered it, he found in its inside a packet in which were dirhams or dinars or a jewel. For whom would that be? So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'Introduce it to the seller, so if he does not recognize it, then the thing is for you. May Allah grant you sustenance with it.'

key_terms.أَضَاحِيّ: Animals sacrificed for Eid al-Adha or other occasions

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I find money inside an animal I bought for sacrifice?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific exception to the general rules of *Luqata* (found property) by treating the contents of a purchased animal as a hidden treasure (*kanz*) rather than lost property. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that if the original owner cannot be identified through the seller, the finder acquires full ownership, reflecting the practical application of divine provision (*rizq*) in commercial transactions.
